assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic physiology of proglucagon-derived peptides and incretins translated into transformative therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity; very large clinical and societal impact with clear originality in physiology and drug development.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, intestinotrophic and metabolic actions) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry identifying active GLP-1(7-36)) are the most defensible core trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's industrial drug-development role is substantial but is more naturally an applied contribution; credit among Habener-linked work is not fully represented in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Basic mechanism confirmed over decades and validated by large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between academic groups on GLP-1 identification are not fully resolved from my knowledge.
Whether industry contributors (Knudsen) should displace an academic laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrated TNF as a dominant cytokine in rheumatoid synovium and that its blockade is effective in patients, proving the concept of targeted cytokine therapy and reshaping treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease and psoriasis. Strong, clear, lasting impact in autoimmune medicine.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the mechanistic discovery in synovial cultures and the first clinical trials of anti-TNF antibody; the pair is a coherent, well-established configuration. Other contributors (for example in TNF biology and antibody engineering) exist but the supplied credit supports a fair two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty-five years of clinical confirmation across diseases; recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Contributions of TNF discoverers and antibody developers outside the supplied names may be argued by others.
I work in rheumatology, so I note the risk of field-familiarity bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, the second messenger cGAMP and STING as a unifying pathway for innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus), and cancer immunology. Conceptually original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP; Barber discovered STING (MITA/ERIS work from other groups is concurrent). Chen and Barber is the cleanest configuration; Ishikawa, Wu and Sun made important contributions but credit sharing is complex.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism well confirmed and in clinical exploration, though therapeutic translation (STING agonists/inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved drugs.
uncertainties: Concurrent independent STING identifications complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics is a transformative method that opened causal circuit-level analysis across neuroscience and physiology, built on microbial rhodopsins; originality and methodological impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The discovery of channelrhodopsin function (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation) make for a difficult three-person limit. I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, acknowledging Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck are also strong.
assessment.maturity: Technology widely adopted for over fifteen years; clinical translation (retinal optogenetics) is only beginning.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six credited names is genuinely contested.
The Nobel award may be viewed as methodological rather than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR/mTOR as the central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing, with major implications for metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunosuppression. Fundamental and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and is the clear first laureate; Sabatini identified mTOR and mTORC1 regulation by amino acids in mammals. Schreiber's work on rapamycin-FKBP12 binding is relevant, but a Hall plus Sabatini configuration is cleaner; Sabatini's later professional controversies are a possible consideration for the committee.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, validated across organisms, and with clinical use of rapalogs.
uncertainties: Whether credit for the mammalian target should include Schreiber or Sabatini's contemporaries (Abraham, Sabers).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, the signalling from ER to nucleus via IRE1/HAC1 and XBP1 splicing, with implications for secretory cell physiology, immunity, neurodegeneration and cancer. Clear, original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori discovered the ER-to-nucleus signalling in yeast and the pathway; Walter's contributions extended to IRE1 and ISRIB, and Mori identified HAC1/ATF6. Others (Kaufman, Ron, Hampton) also contributed, which limits the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive confirmation, and Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: Contributions of Ron, Kaufman and others in mammalian UPR may be seen as omitted.
Direct therapeutic impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, with an approved product class; strong clinical impact and a new therapeutic modality.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed CD19 CAR constructs with costimulatory domains; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials. Zelig Eshhar's foundational CAR concept is not among the supplied names, which weakens the fair-credit configuration.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy confirmed in multiple trials; long-term safety, secondary malignancy and access issues are still evolving.
uncertainties: Missing foundational contributor Eshhar in the supplied credit.
Role of Rosenberg versus June and Sadelain is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-term adult-stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5 stem cells, enabling human disease modelling, drug testing and personalized medicine; high experimental impact across fields.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear leader (Lgr5 stem cells and organoid culture); Sato carried out the key experimental work. A two-person configuration is coherent, though competing organoid approaches (pluripotent-derived) exist.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted, but therapeutic and clinical impact is still maturing.
uncertainties: Maturity of clinical translation is limited.
Overlap with pluripotent stem cell-derived organoid work.
